topics.title: Stanza 1: Drowsy numbness and the happy Dryad

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the nightingale's song leaves the poet in a state of painful, drowsy numbness.
Interpret the allusions to hemlock, Lethe and the Dryad in the opening stanza.
Analyse why the poet longs for wine as a means of escaping the world.
Identify the meaning of Flora, Provencal and Hippocrene in the stanza.

topics.title: Stanza 3: The weariness, the fever and the fret

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the unpleasant aspects of the human condition the poet wishes to escape.
Explain how the poem shows that beauty and love do not last.
Explain how the poet brings out the immortality of the nightingale's song.
Interpret the allusion to Ruth and the image of magic casements.

topics.title: Stanza 8: Forlorn, the return to the self

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the word 'forlorn' tosses the poet back from ecstasy to his sole self.
Evaluate how the closing lines bring out the elusive nature of happiness.

topics.title: The poet, form and poetic devices

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the ode form, apostrophe and oxymoron as used in the poem.
Recall facts about John Keats and recognise sensuous imagery of sound, sight and taste.
